Key Characteristics & Etiology: Viral (Rotavirus) or bacterial enteric infection causing massive watery diarrhea and vomiting
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Invasive or enterotoxigenic mucosal damage leading to severe fluid/electrolyte loss and hypovolemia
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Lethargic/unconscious sunken eyes skin pinch >2s unable to drink; Red Flags: Hypovolemic shock oliguria
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Stool culture serum electrolytes blood urea/creatinine; WHO Plan C: IV Ringer's Lactate/Normal Saline 100 mL/kg + Zinc 10-14 days

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Primary severe nutrient intake deficiency or underlying chronic disease/infection
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Reductive adaptation tissue wasting loss of visceral protein (Kwashiorkor) or subcutaneous fat (Marasmus)
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Marasmus (severe wasting) or Kwashiorkor (bilateral pitting edema flaky-paint rash hair changes); Red Flags: Hypoglycemia <3.0 mmol/L hypothermia sepsis
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: WFH <-3 SD MUAC <115 mm blood glucose electrolytes; WHO 10-Step Plan: 10% Glucose F-75 formula ReSoMol empirical antibiotics

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Hepatotropic viral infection (HAV HBV HCV HDV HEV); Perinatal transmission of HBV carries >90% chronicity risk
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Immune-mediated hepatocyte necrosis resulting in impaired conjugation clearance and synthetic liver failure
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Anorexia nausea right upper quadrant pain jaundice dark urine pale stools; Red Flags: Hepatic encephalopathy INR >2.0
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Serum transaminases (AST/ALT) Bilirubin HBsAg/HBeAg IgM anti-HAV; Supportive care; Neonatal post-exposure: HBIG + HBV vaccine <12h

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Plasmodium falciparum infection transmitted via female Anopheles mosquito bite
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Sequestration of parasitized RBCs in microvasculature causing tissue ischemia inflammation and hemolysis
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: High spike fevers chills rigors pallor splenomegaly; Red Flags: Cerebral malaria (coma/seizures) severe anemia blackwater fever
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Blood film thick/thin smears Rapid Diagnostic Test (RDT) FBC; Intravenous Artesunate (2.4 mg/kg) first-line

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Secondary infection with different Dengue virus serotype (DEN 1-4)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Antibody-dependent enhancement causing severe capillary hyperpermeability plasma leakage and thrombocytopenia
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: High fever positive Tourniquet test petechiae; Red Flags: Plasma leakage (PCV rise >=20%) severe abdominal pain mucosal bleeding DSS shock
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Dengue NS1 antigen positive Thrombocytopenia <100k PCV rise >=20%; Isotonic IV crystalloid resuscitation (5-7 mL/kg/h)

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Ingestion of infective eggs (Ascaris Trichuris) or skin penetration by filariform larvae (Hookworm)
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Adult worms inhabit intestinal lumen causing mechanical obstruction (Ascaris) blood loss (Hookworm) or mucosal inflammation (Trichuris)
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Ascaris: intestinal obstruction; Hookworm: severe iron deficiency anemia; Trichuris: dysentery and rectal prolapse; Pinworm: perianal itch appendicitis
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Stool microscopy for ova/parasites FBC for eosinophilia and anemia; Single dose Oral Albendazole (400 mg) or Mebendazole (500 mg)

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Corynebacterium diphtheriae infection in unimmunized or incompletely immunized children
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Diphtheria exotoxin inhibits protein synthesis causing tissue necrosis and pseudomembrane formation with systemic myocarditis risk
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Sore throat low-grade fever pseudomembrane over tonsils/pharynx 'bull neck' cervical adenopathy; Red Flags: Stridor myocarditis arrhythmia
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Throat swab culture (Löffler/Tellurite medium) Elek toxigenicity test; Immediate Diphtheria Antitoxin (DAT) + IV Penicillin G/Erythromycin

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Invagination of proximal bowel into distal lumen (ileocolic most common); Peaking in infants 3-12 months
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Venous congestion bowel wall edema intestinal obstruction mucosal sloughing and potential bowel necrosis/perforation
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Paroxysmal colicky pain screaming with legs drawn up 'red currant jelly' stool sausage-shaped RUQ mass; Red Flags: Peritonitis shock
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Abdominal Ultrasound (target/doughnut sign); Ultrasound-guided Air or Hydrostatic Contrast Enema reduction

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Inadequate usable calories due to insufficient intake (organic/inorganic) malabsorption or excessive metabolic demand
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Chronic energy deficit resulting in fat mobilization muscle wasting and delayed physical and neurodevelopmental growth
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Weight dropping across >=2 major percentile lines weight-for-height <5th percentile delayed milestones muscle wasting
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Detailed dietary history growth velocity charting FBC U&Es stool elastase tTG; Nutritional rehabilitation + multidisciplinary team

Key Characteristics & Etiology: Delayed introduction of complementary foods (>6 months) or improper early introduction (<4 months) or unfortified diets
Primary Mechanism & Pathophysiology: Transition from exclusive breast milk required to meet increasing iron zinc and caloric demands beyond 6 months
Clinical Manifestations & Red Flags: Growth faltering iron deficiency anemia rickets micronutrient deficiencies recurrent infections
Diagnostic Markers & Primary Management: Nutritional assessment growth charting serum ferritin 25-OH Vitamin D; Infant feeding counseling + exclusive breastfeeding for 6m + timely complementary feeding
